biorxiv.name: bioRxiv
biorxiv.full_name: bioRxiv - The Preprint Server for Biology
biorxiv.description: Free online archive and distribution service for unpublished preprints in the life sciences.

fields.label: Type of result
fields.help: bioRxiv categorizes manuscripts by how the results relate to prior work.

fields.label: Is your manuscript better suited for bioRxiv or medRxiv?
fields.help: openRxiv routes manuscripts to bioRxiv (biology) or medRxiv (clinical/health). Pick the category that best describes your content.
options: Diagnostic tools or medical equipment tested in humans
Epidemiological and/or public health study in humans
Studies linking human gene(s) variant(s) with disease(s) (including small GWAS and UK Biobank n=1)

fields.label: Is your article within scope for bioRxiv?
fields.help: bioRxiv verifies that your article type is in scope for the preprint server. Select the option that best describes it.

fields.label: Subject category / collection
fields.help: Select the single category that best describes your findings.

fields.label: Manuscript title
fields.help: The full title of the manuscript.

fields.label: Abstract
fields.help: Plain-text abstract as it should appear on the bioRxiv abstract page.

fields.label: Authors
fields.help: One author per line, in order. Format: Name | email | affiliation | ORCID | corresponding(yes/no). Mark exactly one author as the corresponding author.

fields.label: Manuscript file
fields.help: Path to the manuscript. Accepted formats: PDF, Word (.docx), or a LaTeX source bundle.

fields.label: Figure / image files
fields.help: Optional. One file per line as 'path | label' (label optional). Uploaded to the figure dropzone.

fields.label: Supplementary files
fields.help: Optional. One file per line as 'path | type | linktext' (these are the only three fields; type and linktext optional). type is the bioRxiv supplemental file-type and must be one of: avi, csv, doc, docx, gif, gz, html, jpg, mov, mp4, mpg, pdf, ppt, pptx, tif, tsv, txt, wmv, xls, xlsx, zip. linktext is the displayed link text. Uploaded to the supplemental dropzone.

fields.label: License / reuse terms
fields.help: Distribution license under which the preprint is posted.

fields.label: Competing interest statement
fields.help: Declare any competing interests. Enter 'The authors have declared no competing interest.' if none.
fields.default: The authors have declared no competing interest.

fields.label: Funding statement
fields.help: Optional. One funder per line as 'Funder name | award1, award2' (awards optional). The funder name must match a FundRef funder, since bioRxiv requires picking an autocomplete suggestion.

fields.label: Data availability links
fields.help: Optional. One URL per line for external datasets or supplementary material at other repositories that pertain to this manuscript. These links are shown to readers once the submission is posted online (e.g. https://www.example.com). Each line must be a valid URL.

fields.label: Is this a revision of an existing bioRxiv preprint?
fields.help: Set to yes if submitting a revised version of a preprint already on bioRxiv.

fields.label: DOI of the existing preprint (if a revision)
fields.help: Only needed when is_revision is yes.

fields.label: Forward to a journal via B2J on posting?
fields.help: bioRxiv-to-Journal (B2J): offer to forward the manuscript to a participating journal.

fields.label: Destination journal for B2J
fields.help: Only needed when transfer_to_journal is yes.

fields.label: All authors consent to deposit and to the chosen license
fields.help: Confirms every author has agreed to deposit the manuscript on bioRxiv under the selected license.

medrxiv.name: medRxiv
medrxiv.full_name: medRxiv - The Preprint Server for Health Sciences
medrxiv.description: Free online archive and distribution server for complete but unpublished manuscripts (preprints) in the medical, clinical, and related health sciences.

fields.label: Subject category
fields.help: Select the single medRxiv subject area that best describes the manuscript.
options: Endocrinology (including Diabetes Mellitus and Metabolic Disease)
Intensive Care and Critical Care Medicine

fields.help: Optional. One URL per line for external datasets or supplementary material at other repositories. On medRxiv the same links populate both the external-dataset and clinical-trial protocol link sections. They are shown to readers once the preprint posts (e.g. https://www.example.com). Each line must be a valid URL.

fields.label: Data availability statement
fields.default: All data produced in the present study are available upon reasonable request to the authors.
fields.help: Free-text description of data availability shown on the medRxiv declarations page.

fields.label: Does the study use human data, samples, or involve human subjects?
fields.help: medRxiv screening question. Answer 'Yes' if the work uses human data/samples or involves human subjects (including public datasets, surveys, patient records, or clinical protocols); otherwise 'No'.

fields.label: Did this work use ONLY simulated data or ONLY openly public data?
fields.help: Only used when human_subjects is 'Yes'. Answer 'Yes' if the work used ONLY simulated data or ONLY data that were openly available to the public before the study began; answer 'No' if any data required application, screening, or registration for access, or otherwise involved human subjects requiring ethics oversight.

fields.label: Source of the openly available data
fields.help: Only used when human_subjects is 'Yes' and public_data_only is 'Yes'. State where the openly available data were originally located (with links, if applicable), e.g. 'The study used ONLY openly available human data that were originally located at: <URL>'.

fields.label: Ethics oversight / approval statement
fields.help: Only used when human_subjects is 'Yes' and public_data_only is 'No'. State the full, non-abbreviated institutional affiliation and name of the ethics oversight body, and whether ethical approval was granted or waived, e.g. 'Ethics committee/IRB of <Full Institution name> gave ethical approval for this work'.

fields.label: Is this manuscript reporting a clinical trial?
fields.help: medRxiv screening question. Select 'Yes' for a registered clinical trial, 'No' for a non-trial study, or 'Not applicable'.

fields.label: Is this a revision of an existing medRxiv preprint?
fields.help: Set to yes if submitting a revised version of a preprint already on medRxiv.

fields.label: Forward to a journal via M2J on posting?
fields.help: medRxiv-to-Journal (M2J): offer to forward the manuscript to a participating journal.

bioinformatics.name: Bioinformatics
bioinformatics.description: Computational molecular biology covering new algorithms, software, databases, and analyses of biological data.
file_type_options: Supplementary Material for Review & Online Publication
Response to Decision letter (Transfer Desk use only)

fields.label: Manuscript type
fields.help: Original Paper: up to 7 pages (approx. 5,000 words, excluding figures); original papers describing new research developments in computational molecular biology, for example new models, algorithms, software involving new methods, biological databases and networks, information services, and their impact on molecular biology or computer science; biological data, as opposed to purely simulated data, must be used. Letter to the Editor: up to 2 pages (approx. 1,300 words, or 1,000 words plus one figure); letters on the broad range of topics covered by the journal, including political, technical, and scientific analyses of issues related to bioinformatics and computational biology, and may include discussion of papers published by the journal. Applications Note: up to 4 pages (approx. 2,600 words, or 2,000 words plus one figure); short descriptions of novel software or new algorithm implementations, databases, and network services (web servers and interfaces); software or data must be freely available to non-commercial users, availability and implementation must be clearly stated in the article, and the name of the application should be included in the title. Review: 3-8 pages (approx. 3,000-6,000 words, excluding figures); most reviews are commissioned, although the editors welcome suggestions from prospective authors, who should in the first instance email a draft or abstract/summary no longer than a page to the editorial office.

fields.label: Manuscript title
fields.help: Full title of the manuscript. For Applications Notes, the name of the application must be included in the title.

fields.label: Abstract
fields.help: Original Papers use a structured abstract with the headings 'Motivation:', 'Results:', 'Availability and implementation:', 'Contact:', and (optional) 'Supplementary information:'.

fields.label: Subject category
fields.help: Please select your manuscript subject category

fields.label: Does your manuscript involve Next Generation Sequencing data analysis?
fields.help: Set to yes if manuscript involves Next Generation Sequencing data analysis.

fields.label: Does your manuscript involve Machine Learning?
fields.help: Set to yes if manuscript involves machine learning.

fields.label: Portal Keywords
fields.help: Portal keywords selected on the ScholarOne keywords step. The vocabulary below is recommended but not required; any term you enter is accepted, with a warning if it is off the list. Choose 3 to 6; enter them comma-separated. List the recommended vocabulary from the command line with `python -m paperpush.venues.bioinformatics`.

fields.label: Keywords
fields.help: Free keywords selected on the ScholarOne keywords step. The vocabulary shared with Portal Keywords is recommended but not required; any term you enter is accepted, with a warning if it is off the list. Choose up to 6; enter them comma-separated. List the recommended vocabulary from the command line with `python -m paperpush.venues.bioinformatics`.

fields.label: Authors
fields.help: One author per line, in order. Format: email | prefix | name | institution | country/region | city | corresponding(yes/no). Each author is added on ScholarOne by email lookup, so an email is required for every author. If the email is already registered the remaining columns are ignored; if it is not, the author is created from the prefix, name, institution, country/region, and city. Mark exactly one corresponding author. Prefix must be one of: Dr., Miss, Mr., Mrs., Ms., Prof., Mx. Institution and country/region are picked from ScholarOne drop-down lists, so spell them as they appear there.

fields.label: Cover letter
fields.help: Mandatory; submissions without a cover letter may be editorially rejected. Must explain the paper's suitability, disclose any related preprints, dissertations, or manuscripts and how this work differs, and declare conflicts of interest and any generative AI/LLM use.

fields.label: Manuscript file
fields.help: Path to the manuscript. A PDF is typically uploaded for review; Word (.docx) or LaTeX source is required for the final accepted manuscript. The page and word limits depend on the article type: Original Paper up to 7 pages (approx. 5,000 words), Letter to the Editor up to 2 pages (approx. 1,300 words), Applications Note up to 4 pages (approx. 2,600 words), and Review up to 8 pages (approx. 3,000-6,000 words). These are encoded in max_pages_by, keyed on the article_type field.

fields.label: Figures
fields.help: Optional. One path per line. Provide high-resolution figure files. Each uploads with the 'Figure' file type.

fields.label: Tables
fields.help: Optional. One path per line. Tables uploaded as separate files, each with the 'Table' file type.

fields.label: Number of pages
fields.help: Total number of pages in the manuscript.

fields.label: Number of tables
fields.help: Total number of tables in the manuscript.

fields.label: Number of figures
fields.help: Total number of figures in the manuscript.

fields.label: Supplementary materials
fields.help: Optional. Supplementary materials should be combined into a single file and cannot be altered or replaced after acceptance.

fields.label: Data availability statement
fields.help: Required for all papers. Describe and provide the means of access to the underlying data, linking to the data or providing a unique identifier. Data sets cited in the manuscript should also appear in the reference list.

fields.label: Conflict of interest statement
fields.help: All authors must disclose competing interests at submission. The corresponding author is responsible for ensuring all authors' conflicts are declared. Enter 'None declared.' if there are none.

fields.label: Funding statement
fields.help: Funding sources and grant numbers.

fields.label: Ethics statement
fields.help: Where ethically relevant, confirm the research followed applicable international and local guidelines and any required approvals were obtained.

fields.label: Author contributions (CRediT)
fields.help: Describe each author's contribution using the CRediT contributor roles taxonomy.

fields.label: Generative AI use disclosure
fields.help: Disclose any use of generative AI or LLM tools in both the cover letter and the Methods or Acknowledgements section, with sufficient detail. AI tools cannot be listed as authors.

fields.label: Reviewers
fields.help: One reviewer per line. Format: name | email | stance | reason. stance must be 'recommended' or 'opposed' (case-insensitive); reason is optional (a free-text justification shown to the editor). At least 4 recommended reviewers are required; opposed reviewers do not count toward that minimum. Each reviewer is added through the ScholarOne 'Add Reviewer' form, which splits the name into first/last on the last space, so write the name as 'First Last'.

fields.label: Is there funding to report for this submission?
fields.help: Declaration answered on the final submission step. Set to yes if there is funding to report for this submission. Report the funding sources and grant numbers in the funding statement.

fields.label: Is this a resubmission of a manuscript which was previously submitted under a different manuscript number?
fields.help: Declaration answered on the final submission step. Set to yes if this manuscript was previously submitted under a different manuscript number. When yes, provide that number in previous_manuscript_id.

fields.label: If yes, what is the manuscript ID of the previous submission?
fields.help: Only needed when resubmission is yes. The manuscript ID (manuscript number) of the previous submission.

fields.label: Do you or your co-authors have any conflict of interest?
fields.help: Declaration answered on the final submission step. Set to yes if you or any co-author has a conflict of interest. When yes, state it in conflict_of_interest_details.

fields.label: If yes, please state your conflict of interest:
fields.help: Only needed when has_conflict_of_interest is yes. State the conflict(s) of interest for you and your co-authors.

fields.label: Have you cited any works that are unpublished or in press?
fields.help: Declaration answered on the final submission step. Set to yes if you have cited any unpublished or in-press works; if so, they must be uploaded as a 'Supplementary Material for Review Only' file so reviewers can understand their relation to the manuscript. No means no such works were cited.

fields.label: Is an algorithm or software central to the paper?
fields.help: Reproducibility checklist item answered on the final declarations step. Set to yes if an algorithm or software is central to the paper.

fields.label: The text of the article includes a link to the code in an open-source repository (e.g., GitHub).
fields.help: Reproducibility checklist item answered on the final declarations step. Set to yes if the manuscript text itself contains a link to the code in an open-source repository such as GitHub.

fields.label: Please provide the link to the repository below (optional):
fields.help: Optional. The URL of the open-source code repository (e.g., a GitHub repository). When provided, it must be a valid http/https URL.

fields.label: The software can be installed from an open package repository (e.g. Bioconda, PyPI, Bioconductor) or contains an extensive installation guide and all software dependencies are listed.
fields.help: Reproducibility checklist item. Set to yes if the software is installable from an open package repository, or if it provides an extensive installation guide and lists all software dependencies.

fields.label: Someone that is not familiar with the tool has tested its installation and use prior to submission.
fields.help: Reproducibility checklist item. Set to yes if a person unfamiliar with the tool tested its installation and use before submission.

fields.label: The software repository contains a link to a test dataset, and the README includes the instructions to run the method on the test dataset, with the input and output clearly described.
fields.help: Reproducibility checklist item. Set to yes if the repository links to a test dataset and the README documents how to run the method on it, with the input and output clearly described.

fields.label: The data used in the manuscript is clearly documented.
fields.help: Reproducibility checklist item. Set to yes if the sources of all datasets (including training and evaluation datasets) are provided, all datasets are versioned, and the source and process of ground-truth annotations are provided.

fields.label: Please provide the link(s)/accessions/reference(s) to the data sources:
fields.help: Optional. Links, accession numbers, or references to the data sources used in the manuscript. Accession numbers and citations are accepted in addition to URLs, so no URL format is enforced.

fields.label: Is this a Machine Learning / Deep Learning paper?
fields.help: Set to yes if the manuscript is a machine learning (ML) or deep learning (DL) paper. When yes, three additional checklist questions about train-test splits, dataset transformations, and performance metrics are answered on the same step.

fields.label: The details of train-test splits or cross-validation folds are explicitly mentioned in the manuscript.
fields.help: Only applicable when is_ml_dl_paper is yes. Set to yes if the manuscript explicitly describes the train-test splits or cross-validation folds.

fields.label: All transformations of the dataset from its raw form to the form used in the model are reported, and the corresponding pre-processing code is provided.
fields.help: Only applicable when is_ml_dl_paper is yes. Set to yes if every transformation of the dataset from its raw form to the form used in the model (for instance, treatment of missing data and normalization) is reported and the corresponding pre-processing code is provided.

fields.label: All metrics used to assess and compare model performance are provided along with uncertainty estimates.
fields.help: Only applicable when is_ml_dl_paper is yes. Set to yes if all metrics used to assess and compare model performance (e.g., accuracy, area under the receiver operating characteristic curve) are provided along with uncertainty estimates (e.g., confidence intervals, standard deviations).

fields.label: Is this manuscript posted as a preprint?
fields.help: Set to yes if a version is posted on a preprint server such as bioRxiv. The manuscript must not be under consideration at more than one journal simultaneously.

fields.label: Preprint DOI (if applicable)
fields.help: Only needed when is_preprint is yes. Update the preprint with the published DOI if accepted.

nucleic_acids_research.name: Nucleic Acids Research
nucleic_acids_research.description: Leading research in nucleic acids, including their chemistry, biology, and applications, and computational and structural studies of nucleic acids and their interactions.
file_type_options: Supplementary data - NOT for compiled PDF (eg video, Excel, large data files)
Data - for review, not for publication

fields.label: Manuscript type
fields.help: The type of manuscript being submitted to Nucleic Acids Research, selected on the first submission step.

fields.label: Key Points
fields.help: Exactly 3 bullet points summarizing the manuscript's contribution to the field, one per line, 100 characters maximum per point. Entered in the Key Points box on page 1, after the abstract.

fields.label: Keywords
fields.help: Required. Provide 3 to 5 free keywords describing the manuscript, comma-separated. Entered on the ScholarOne keywords step; any term is accepted.

fields.label: Authors
fields.help: One author per line, in order. Format: email | prefix | name | institution | country/region | city | corresponding(yes/no). Each author is added on ScholarOne by email lookup, so an email is required for every author. If the email is already registered the remaining columns are ignored; if it is not, the author is created from the prefix, name, institution, country/region, and city. Mark exactly one corresponding author. Prefix must be one of: Dr, Prof., Mx . Institution and country/region are picked from ScholarOne drop-down lists, so spell them as they appear there.

fields.label: Funding
fields.help: Optional. One funder per line, formatted 'funder | grant id' (the grant id optional). Drives the 'Add Funder' step on the declarations page; leave empty to declare no funding.

fields.label: Referees
fields.help: One referee per line. Format: name | email | stance | reason. stance must be 'recommended' or 'opposed' (case-insensitive); a reason is required for every referee. At least 6 recommended referees are required; at most 3 opposed referees are allowed (opposed referees do not count toward the minimum). Each referee is added through the ScholarOne 'Add Referee' form, which splits the name into first/last on the last space, so write the name as 'First Last'.

fields.label: Manuscript category
fields.help: Select the Nucleic Acids Research manuscript category on the declarations step. Category descriptions are linked from the submission form.
options: Chemical Biology and Nucleic Acid Chemistry

fields.label: Is this manuscript a resubmission of previous work?
fields.help: Set to yes if this manuscript is a resubmission of previous work.

fields.label: Manuscript ID of the previous submission (if a resubmission)
fields.help: Only needed when is_resubmission is yes: the manuscript ID of the previous submission.

fields.label: Conflict of interest statement
fields.help: Disclose any conflict of interest for you or your co-authors. Leave empty or enter 'None declared.' if there are none; any other text answers the conflict-of-interest question 'Yes' and is provided as the details.

fields.label: If this is a resubmission or revision, has the author list been altered?
fields.help: For a resubmission or revision, whether the author list has been altered. Use 'Not Applicable' for a new submission.

fields.label: If the author list has been altered, please provide details
fields.help: Only needed when author_list_altered is 'Yes': describe how the author list changed.

fields.label: Should this manuscript be published back-to-back with another?
fields.help: Set to yes if this manuscript should be published back-to-back with another manuscript.

fields.label: First three authors of the accompanying manuscript (if back-to-back)
fields.help: Only needed when back_to_back is yes: list the first three authors of the accompanying manuscript.

fields.label: Does the manuscript contain a Novel Method?
fields.help: Set to yes if the manuscript contains a novel method.

fields.label: Brief description of the novel method (if any)
fields.help: Only needed when novel_method is yes: briefly describe the novel method.

fields.label: Is this manuscript accompanied by supplementary material for publication online only?
fields.help: Set to yes if the manuscript is accompanied by supplementary material intended for online-only publication.

fields.label: Source of funding for publication charges
fields.help: Required. State the source of funding for your publication charges (Nucleic Acids Research is a fully open access journal).

fields.label: Institution verification status
fields.help: On the authors step, OUP asks you to confirm your institution. Choose 'verified' if you confirm your institution is verified, 'not in list' if you have an institution but it is not available in the list, or 'N/A entered' if you do not have an institution and have entered 'N/A'.

fields.label: Data availability statement
fields.help: Required. Paste the data availability statement from the manuscript text, including any accession numbers, login details, or reviewer tokens.

fields.label: Data deposition: which of the following does the manuscript use or report?
fields.help: Select every listed data type the manuscript uses or reports; access to such data must be given at submission. Selected types are answered 'Yes' and the rest 'No'. Comma-separated; leave empty if none apply.
options: New genome expression or sequencing data (ChIP-seq, RNA-seq)
New genome-wide binding/interaction data or genome-wide mutation data
Molecular behaviour studies (biological NMR spectroscopy data)
Structures of nucleosides, nucleotides, other small molecules
Synthetic nucleic acid oligonucleotides including siRNAs or shRNAs
Gel images, micrographs, graphs, and tables

arxiv.name: arXiv
arxiv.full_name: arXiv - Open-access archive for scholarly articles
arxiv.description: Free distribution service and open-access archive for preprints in physics, mathematics, computer science, quantitative biology, quantitative finance, statistics, and more.

fields.label: Primary archive
fields.help: The top-level arXiv archive your work belongs to. This is the value of the submission form's archive drop-down (#select_arch), so use the archive code (e.g. 'cs' for Computer Science, 'q-bio' for Quantitative Biology, 'stat' for Statistics).

fields.label: Primary subject category
fields.help: The specific subject class within the primary archive, as the value of the form's subject-class drop-down (#select_sc). Use the full category code, e.g. 'cs.AI' (Artificial Intelligence), 'q-bio.GN' (Genomics), or 'stat.ML' (Machine Learning). It must belong to the chosen primary_archive. See https://arxiv.org/category_taxonomy for the full list.

fields.label: Cross-list archives
fields.help: Optional. Additional top-level archives to cross-list the paper under, comma-separated (e.g. 'cs, stat'). Same archive codes as primary_archive, with no limit on how many. Each entry is paired positionally with the matching entry in crosslist_categories and added on the metadata step after the primary category.

fields.label: Cross-list categories
fields.help: Optional. Additional subject categories to cross-list the paper under, comma-separated (e.g. 'cs.LG, stat.ML'). Same category codes as primary_category, with no limit on how many. Each entry is paired positionally with the matching entry in crosslist_archives and added on the metadata step after the primary category.

fields.label: License
fields.help: Distribution license for the submission. The arXiv perpetual, non-exclusive license is the minimum arXiv requires; the Creative Commons options grant broader reuse. Note: the runner currently selects the license radio captured in the recording (the first option); full license-by-name selection is pending, so confirm the license in the browser before the final submit.

fields.label: Title
fields.help: The full title of the article.

fields.label: Authors
fields.help: One author per line, in order. Format: Name | email | affiliation | ORCID | corresponding(yes/no). arXiv records authors as a single comma-separated list of names, so only the Name column is used for the metadata field; mark exactly one corresponding author (the account submitting). Use the form 'Firstname Lastname' for each name.

fields.label: Abstract
fields.help: Plain-text abstract as it should appear on the arXiv abstract page.

fields.label: Manuscript file
fields.help: Path to the submission. arXiv prefers a LaTeX source bundle (a .zip or .tar.gz of the .tex, figures, and .bbl); a single PDF is accepted for PDF-only submissions. The file is uploaded, processed, and confirmed on the Files step.

fields.label: Comments
fields.help: Optional. Free-text comments shown on the abstract page, conventionally the page/figure count and notes (e.g. '10 pages, 4 figures; submitted to JOSS').

fields.label: Report number
fields.help: Optional. Author-assigned report or preprint number, if any.

fields.label: Journal reference
fields.help: Optional. Full bibliographic reference once the article has been published in a journal.

fields.label: ACM classification
fields.help: Optional. ACM Computing Classification System code(s), semicolon-separated (e.g. 'F.2.2; I.2.7'). Relevant mainly for cs submissions.

fields.label: MSC classification
fields.help: Optional. Mathematics Subject Classification code(s), comma-separated (e.g. '14J60, 14F05'). Relevant mainly for math submissions.

fields.label: DOI
fields.help: Optional. DOI of a published version of this article, if one exists.

nature.name: Nature
nature.full_name: Nature - International weekly journal of science
nature.description: Weekly multidisciplinary journal publishing peer-reviewed research of outstanding significance across all fields of science and technology, alongside news and commentary.

fields.label: Manuscript type
fields.help: The submission category, selected on the opening eJournalPress manuscript-type page. Choose one of the listed options exactly. For Nature, the type also names the research area and whether this is a full submission or a presubmission enquiry (e.g. 'Biological Sciences - Article').

fields.label: Manuscript title
fields.help: The full title of the manuscript, typed into the eJournalPress title box.

fields.label: Abstract
fields.help: Plain-text abstract, typed into the eJournalPress abstract box.

fields.label: Subject categories
fields.help: Nature subject classification, chosen from the dependent menus on the eJournalPress subjects step. The category tree is not a fixed depth: every branch has a level 1 and level 2, and some continue deeper, to as many as six levels. Format each category as its level names joined by ' | ' (subject_level_1 | subject_level_2 | ...), giving as many levels as the chosen branch offers; level 1 and level 2 are required and the deeper levels are optional. Provide between two and five categories in total, each on its own line. Each part must match a category name exactly. List the valid values from the command line with python -m paperpush.venues.nature: run it with no arguments for the level-1 categories, then add the chosen names one at a time (a quoted level-1 name for its level-2 categories, a quoted level-1 and level-2 pair for its level-3 categories, a level-1/level-2/level-3 triple for its level-4 categories) to drill deeper. Example: python -m paperpush.venues.nature 'Biological sciences | Biochemistry | Proteomics'.

fields.label: Authors
fields.help: One author per line, in order. Format: title | first name | last name | email | institution | country/region | city | corresponding(yes/no). The title is the name prefix selected in the eJournalPress drop-down (e.g. Mr, Ms, Dr, Professor). City is optional. The author marked corresponding=yes fills the corresponding-author sub-form; the boxes that the signed-in account already pre-filled (typically first name, last name, email) are left untouched. Country/region is matched to the eJournalPress drop-down by name (US/USA map to 'United States', UK to 'United Kingdom').

fields.label: Manuscript file
fields.help: Path to the manuscript, uploaded as the 'Article File' on the eJournalPress upload step.

fields.label: Cover letter
fields.help: Optional. Path to the cover letter, uploaded as the 'Author Cover Letter' on the eJournalPress upload step.

fields.label: Figure files
fields.help: Optional. Main figures, one per line as 'path | title | color'. Every column after the path is optional. Each file uploads on the eJournalPress step with the 'Figure' file type. The title names the figure on the per-object metadata step (e.g. 'Figure 1', 'Figure 2A'), falling back to the file name when blank. The color is the per-figure color choice ('color' or 'bw', defaulting to 'color'). Example: 'figs/fig1.eps | Figure 1 | color'.

fields.label: Table files
fields.help: Optional. Main tables uploaded as separate files, one per line as 'path | title' (the title is optional). Each file uploads with the 'Table' file type. Example: 'tables/table1.xlsx | Table 1'.

fields.label: Supplementary information files
fields.help: Optional. Supplementary information files, one per line as 'path | title | description'. Every column after the path is optional. Each file uploads with the 'Supplementary Information' file type. eJournalPress has no distinct supplementary-figure type, so supplementary figures belong here. The title names the object on the per-object metadata step; the description is optional. Example: 'supp/supp_methods.pdf | Supplementary Information | Extended methods'.

fields.label: Supplementary table files
fields.help: Optional. Supplementary tables, one per line as 'path | title | description'. Every column after the path is optional. Each file uploads with the 'Supplementary Table' file type. The title names the object on the per-object metadata step; the description is optional. Example: 'supp/supp_table1.xlsx | Supplementary Table 1 | Source measurements'.

fields.label: Other files
fields.help: Optional. Any further eJournalPress files that are not main figures, main tables, supplementary information, or supplementary tables (use the dedicated fields above for those). One per line as 'path | type | title | extra'; every column after the path is optional. The type must be one of the listed file types; when omitted the eJournalPress default is left in place. The title names a figure or supplementary object on the per-object metadata step; the extra column is a figure's color ('color' or 'bw') or a supplementary file's description. Example: 'data/source_fig1.zip | Source Data |  | Raw gels'.

fields.label: Are you the corresponding author?
fields.help: Whether you (the submitting account holder) are the corresponding author. Answer yes or no.

fields.label: Gender of corresponding author
fields.help: Optional. Your gender, asked by eJournalPress only when you (the submitting account holder) are the corresponding author (are_you_corresponding: yes). Choose one of the listed options, or leave blank to skip. Ignored when are_you_corresponding is no.

fields.label: Code availability statement
fields.help: Optional. Code availability statement for the eJournalPress Code Ocean / code-deposition step. Leave blank to decline (the default: no Code Ocean capsule created). When provided, eJournalPress is told a Code Ocean capsule has been created and this text (up to 4000 characters) is entered as the code availability statement.

fields.label: Competing interests
fields.help: Nature Portfolio requires every submission to declare competing financial and/or non-financial interests. Answer 'no' if the authors have no competing interests, or 'yes' if they do (in which case list them in 'competing_interests_statement' and in a paragraph at the end of the manuscript).

fields.label: Competing interests statement
fields.help: Optional. Used only when 'competing_interests' is 'yes': the paragraph describing the competing interests, typed into the eJournalPress statement box.

fields.label: Published or under consideration elsewhere
fields.help: Whether any of the results/data/figures in this manuscript have been published, or are under consideration for publication, elsewhere. Answer 'no' (the default) or 'yes'; if 'yes', explain in 'dual_publication_statement' why it is not dual publication.

fields.label: Prior/concurrent publication statement
fields.help: Optional. Used only when 'dual_publication' is 'yes': identify the results/data/figures taken from other published or pending manuscripts and explain why this does not constitute dual publication.

fields.label: Peer-review anonymization
fields.help: Optional. Whether author information is shown to reviewers. 'single-anonymized' shows author information to reviewers (the default); 'double-anonymized' hides it, in which case all identifying information must be removed from the files and placed in the cover letter (see https://www.nature.com/documents/nr-double-blind-peer-review.pdf). Left at the form default when blank.

fields.label: Comments to the editor
fields.help: Optional. Additional information for the editor, typed into the eJournalPress comments box: previous manuscript numbers for earlier versions, suggested or excluded referees, or (for a presubmission enquiry) the references used.

nature_biotech.name: Nature Biotechnology
nature_biotech.description: Publishes peer-reviewed research and analysis on the science and business of biotechnology, covering the application of biological systems to therapeutics, diagnostics, agriculture, and related areas.

fields.help: The submission category, selected on the opening eJournalPress manuscript-type page. Choose one of the listed options exactly.

Optional. Supplementary information files, one per line as 'path | title | description'. Every column after the path is optional. Each file uploads with the 'Supplemental & Additional Information' file type. eJournalPress has no distinct supplementary-figure type, so supplementary figures belong here. The title names the object on the per-object metadata step; the description is optional. Example: 'supp/supp_methods.pdf | Supplementary Information | Extended methods'.

nature_methods.name: Nature Methods
nature_methods.description: Publishes peer-reviewed novel methods and significant improvements to techniques across the life sciences, including their development, validation, and application.

fields.help: The submission category, selected on the opening eJournalPress manuscript-type page. Choose one of the listed options exactly.

Nature subject classification, chosen from the dependent menus on the eJournalPress subjects step. The category tree is not a fixed depth: every branch has a level 1 and level 2, and some continue deeper, to as many as six levels. Format each category as its level names joined by ' | ' (subject_level_1 | subject_level_2 | ...), giving as many levels as the chosen branch offers; level 1 and level 2 are required and the deeper levels are optional. Provide between two and five categories in total, each on its own line. Each part must match a category name exactly. List the valid values from the command line with python -m paperpush.venues.nature_methods: run it with no arguments for the level-1 categories, then add the chosen names one at a time (a quoted level-1 name for its level-2 categories, a quoted level-1 and level-2 pair for its level-3 categories, a level-1/level-2/level-3 triple for its level-4 categories) to drill deeper. Example: python -m paperpush.venues.nature_methods 'Biological sciences | Biochemistry | Proteomics'.

Optional. Supplementary information files, one per line as 'path | title | description'. Every column after the path is optional. Each file uploads with the 'Supplementary and Additional Material' file type. eJournalPress has no distinct supplementary-figure type, so supplementary figures belong here. The title names the object on the per-object metadata step; the description is optional. Example: 'supp/supp_methods.pdf | Supplementary Information | Extended methods'.

fields.label: Article type

fields.label: Manuscript title

fields.label: Abstract

fields.label: Keywords

fields.label: Authors

The author marked corresponding=yes must be the submitting account holder (Editorial Manager pre-fills that author); their pre-filled row is edited to fill in any missing details. Every other line is added through the '+Add Another Author' form. Country is mapped to the Editorial Manager country drop-down (e.g. USA/US/United States all map to 'us').

fields.label: Manuscript file

fields.label: Cover letter

fields.label: Declaration of Interests file

fields.label: Figure / image files
fields.help: Optional. One figure file per line as 'path | label' (label optional and unused at upload). Each is uploaded as a separate attachment with the 'Figure' item type on the Editorial Manager 'Attach Files' step.

fields.label: Related work in press or under consideration elsewhere?
fields.help: Cell asks whether you or any co-author has work related to this manuscript in press or under consideration elsewhere. Answer 'Yes' or 'No'.

fields.label: Does the manuscript report original code?
fields.help: Cell asks whether the manuscript reports original computer code, algorithms, or computational models. Set to yes to declare original code (then fill in code_url).

fields.label: Original code repository URL
fields.help: Only used when original_code is yes. URL of the repository where the original code is available (e.g. a GitHub link).

fields.label: Alternate contact email
fields.help: Optional. An alternate contact email Cell can use if the corresponding author is unavailable.

fields.label: Funding statement
fields.help: Optional. One funder per line as 'Funder name | award1, award2' (awards optional). The funder name must match an Editorial Manager funder, since the funder box only accepts a picked autocomplete suggestion. Leave empty to mark funding information as not available.

fields.label: Suggested / opposed reviewers
fields.help: Optional. One reviewer per line. Format: name | email | institution | stance | reason. stance is 'suggested' or 'opposed' (case-insensitive, default 'suggested'); email, institution, and reason are optional. Write the name as 'First Last'; the Editorial Manager reviewer form splits it into given/family name on the last space. Each line is added through the '+Add Suggested Reviewer' or '+Add Opposed Reviewer' form, which mirrors the author form.

fields.label: Submission declarations confirmed
fields.help: Confirms the standard Cell submission declarations (the paper conforms to all requirements, all contributors are listed, all authors have seen the manuscript, and status updates will be shared). The runner checks these boxes only when this is yes.

fields.label: Open access
fields.help: On the Publishing Options step shown after 'Build PDF for Approval', Cell offers an open-access publishing model that carries an article-publishing charge. Choose 'Yes' to select open access or 'No' to keep the standard (subscription) model. The runner opens the Publishing Options popup and applies this choice best-effort.

fields.label: Manuscript title

fields.label: Manuscript short title

fields.label: Suggested / opposed reviewers
fields.help: Optional. One reviewer per line. Format: name | email | institution | stance | reason. stance is 'suggested' or 'opposed' (case-insensitive, default 'suggested'); email, institution, and reason are optional. Write the name as 'First Last'; the Editorial Manager reviewer form splits it into given/family name on the last space. Each line is added through the '+Add Suggested Reviewer' or '+Add Opposed Reviewer' form, which mirrors the author form.

fields.label: Competing interests statement
fields.help: Competing-interests statement for the PLOS declarations page. Typed verbatim into the 'Competing Interests' box. If there are no competing interests, state so explicitly (e.g. 'The authors have declared that no competing interests exist.').

fields.label: Data availability statement
fields.help: Data-availability statement for the PLOS declarations page. Typed verbatim into the 'Data Availability' box. Describe where the data underlying the results can be found, or state why it cannot be shared.

fields.label: Previous interactions with PLOS
fields.help: Optional. Leave blank if there were none. When set, the 'I have had previous interactions...' box is checked on the PLOS declarations page and this text is filled in as the explanation.

fields.label: Prior submission / consideration history
fields.help: Optional. Leave blank if not applicable. When set, the 'This manuscript was...' box is checked on the PLOS declarations page and this text is filled in as the explanation.

fields.label: Preprint DOI
fields.help: Optional. DOI of preprint. If no preprint, leave empty.

fields.label: Related Work, Copyright, & Dual Submission
fields.help: PLOS asks: have any of the results, data, or figures in this manuscript been published elsewhere, or are they under consideration for publication elsewhere? If no, enter 'No'. If yes, identify which results, data, or figures were taken from other published or pending manuscripts and explain why inclusion here does not constitute dual publication; upload a copy of the related work as a 'Related Manuscript' file type (reviewers may be asked to comment on the overlap); and provide the image source, copyright license information, and any permissions received for figures or material adapted from copyrighted material, uploading permissions documents as an 'Other' file type.

fields.label: Funding country
fields.help: Country of the funding source, selected on the PLOS financial-disclosure step's country drop-down. Required when a funding statement is given. Pick the country name; the runner matches it against the drop-down's options.

fields.label: Human participants, data, specimens, or tissue
fields.help: PLOS asks whether the study involved human participants, data, specimens, or tissue. Answer 'No' (the default) or 'Yes'. When 'Yes', the runner selects the affirmative option and checks the three human-subjects confirmation boxes on the declarations page.

fields.label: Authors

fields.label: Data availability statement

fields.label: Acknowledgements

fields.label: Research funding

fields.label: Funding sources

fields.label: Supplementary Material

fields.label: Suggested reviewers

fields.label: Excluded reviewers

fields.label: Comments to the editor

fields.label: Abstract
fields.help: Plain-text abstract of the paper.

fields.label: Secondary topics

fields.label: Countries of institutions

fields.label: PDF

fields.label: Technical supplement

fields.label: Media supplement

fields.label: Code and data supplement

fields.label: LaTeX source files

fields.label: Supplementary material

fields.label: Research data statement
